withdraw.missing: A relation between a road user and the signal head that faces it: which vehicular signal head's face is directed at a given pedestrian (the head's face orientation, or a road-user-faces-device relation), so that the head named by 'facing such a signal' is tied to the subject. The only reading the vocabulary allows is the pedestrian's heading compared with the line to the head's location (kin.heading, kin.position, dev.position). That says only that the pedestrian looks toward the head. It does not say that the head's face is addressed to the pedestrian. The gate also does not accept that comparison as tying the device variable to the subject (UNANCHORED_VARIABLE, run twice, including with the comparisons rewritten without products). The anchors the gate accepts do not carry the words. dev.governs ties a device only to travel regions. A vehicular head that a crossing pedestrian faces governs the approach lanes of traffic moving parallel to that pedestrian, or the junction itself. It does not govern the roadway the pedestrian steps onto. Requiring the faced head to govern the region entered would leave the duty unengaged in the ordinary case: a pedestrian at a corner facing the far-side head for parallel traffic and stepping into the cross street. Tying it by a distance to some governed region would add a condition the words do not state. The span decides which road users the steady red alone addresses: the pedestrians the duty concerns.
nearest: dev.position: 'location of the device head / sign face' (a location only, with no orientation of the face, so it cannot say whom the face addresses)

dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... never ... a region no vehicle travels in' (it relates a device to regions, not to the pedestrian facing it; and the faced vehicular head does not govern the roadway the pedestrian enters)
kin.heading: 'direction the body points' (the pedestrian's own direction, not the direction of the signal face)
